title: Cohorted Access Probation Rollout: RBAC v2 Pilot & SIEM Evidence Plan
content:
Purpose
This is a working plan for a staged RBAC v2 rollout that uses temporary, monitored "probation cohorts" to gather evidence and telemetry for SIEM export and automated attestation. The goal is to reduce blast radius while collecting high-fidelity audit signals that validate policy behavior and entitlement mapping before full conversion.

Why a probation/cohort approach
- RBAC v2 changes are broad and interact with many services (console, API, Dedicated control plane).
- We want deterministic, testable windows where we can observe permission resolution, false-deny/false-allow events, and collect end-to-end evidence for compliance teams.
- Cohorts let us tune transformation rules incrementally (attribute mappings, temporal grants, delegation).

High-level rollout phases
1) Discovery: define critical surfaces and candidate cohorts (2 weeks)
   - Identify 6 candidate services with most critical entitlements (console routes, billing APIs, model-deploy, private-config, infra-provision, support-tools).
   - Export current permission footprints, top-callers, and recent role-change events.

2) Pilot cohort (week 1–6): small group (10–25 users/devices) on the new RBAC path with probation tokens (4 weeks observation)
   - Apply RBAC v2 on request path using gateway-side "probation" header that routes to shadow/evaluate mode for non-authorized actions.
   - Collect shadow vs live decision delta and full evidence bundle for every evaluated request.

3) Evidence automation & SIEM mapping (parallel to pilot)
   - Build evidence enrichment pipeline that: normalizes audit events, attaches role-resolution trace, and emits SIEM-ready events with sampling flags.
   - Validate schema in Splunk/Elastic and iterate.

4) Graduated cohorts (weeks 7–14): expand to teams and service types after threshold pass rates
   - Use cohort success gating: false-deny rate < 0.2%, false-allow rate near 0, and no high-severity operational impact in 7 days.

5) Production cutover and post-cut monitoring (weeks 15–20)
   - Stop probation routing, enable enforcement, keep elevated telemetry retention for 30 days, then downsample.

Core mechanisms and instrumentation
- Probation tokens: short-lived, auditable header inserted at ingress. Contains cohort id, experiment id, start timestamp. Not to be used for auth decisions; only for routing into shadow/compare pipelines.
- Decision traces: every auth evaluation emits a compact trace record (resolver path, matched principals, attribute-lookups, cache-hit).
- Evidence bundle: {"event_id", "request_ts", "caller", "resolved_roles", "policy_version", "decision", "resolver_trace", "raw_request_meta"} (store as NDJSON to evidence bucket).
- Sampling and retention: all probation events are retained in full for 30 days; a 1-in-50 sample of non-probation events taken for baseline comparison.

SIEM export schema (draft)
- Field mapping guideline (SIEM fields on left -> Redwood event keys on right):
  - event.time -> request_ts
  - event.id -> event_id
  - subject.id -> caller
  - object.resource -> resource_path
  - action -> request_action
  - authorization.decision -> decision (ALLOW/DENY/SHADOW_ALLOW/SHADOW_DENY)
  - authorization.policy_version -> policy_version
  - evidence.cohort -> cohort_id
  - evidence.probation -> true|false
  - trace.resolver_path -> resolver_trace (compressed)
  - sampling.rate -> sampling_rate

- Example NDJSON event (as raw text for validation):
{ "event.time": "2024-09-19T18:12:03Z", "event.id": "evt-20240919-7c9f", "subject.id": "alice@redwood.com", "object.resource": "/v1/models/deploy", "action": "model.deploy", "authorization.decision": "SHADOW_DENY", "authorization.policy_version": "rbac-v2-2024-09-12", "evidence.cohort": "pilot-1", "evidence.probation": "true", "trace.resolver_path": "policy->attribute-resolver:roleset-17->cache:miss->decision:deny", "sampling.rate": "1/1" }

Evidence automation & QA playbook (working checklist)
- For each probation event: capture evidence bundle -> push to evidence-bucket -> enrich with enrichment-service (user-directory snapshots, role-hash, recent-priv-change) -> run deterministic QA checks
- QA checks: policy-version matches expected, resolver trace exists, resource canonicalized, user identity resolved to an SCIM id, if DENY then check whether a fallback policy was invoked
- Auto-labeling: if an event passes QA and has zero operational impact for 7 days, tag as "safe" and propose automated migration for equivalent historical GRANTs
- Escalation path: any DENY that causes a 5xx or operational incident triggers immediate rollback to previous policy for that cohort and pager notify to sec-oncall

Operational integrations
- Console: add probation banner and explain shadow mode. Allow users in cohort to file quick feedback entries that attach to evidence events ("I needed access to X to complete Y").
- CI/CD: require a successful cohort pass for infra-modifying PRs touching entitlement config.
- Dedicated & Private: ensure probation header is respected by on-prem agents; evidence-bucket connector runs inside customer network for Private deployments (configurable).

Monitoring and success metrics (example thresholds)
- False-deny rate: target < 0.2% for pilot services over 2 weeks
- False-allow rate: target < 0.01%
- Evidence completeness score: 95% (must include resolver_trace + user id + policy_version)
- Time-to-detect high-severity denial: mean < 10 minutes (alerting via SIEM)

Open questions / risks (WIP)
- How do we handle external SSO sessions where identity snapshots may not be available for historical attestation? (workaround: snapshot at auth-time and include scim hash)
- Data residency for Private deployments: evidence-bucket connectors must support per-region retention rules; who owns the connector certs?
- Performance overhead: decision-trace and evidence packaging add latency. We need to quantify p50/p95 impact and introduce async collection paths for high-throughput endpoints.
- SIEM volume: full probation retention will spike SIEM ingest. Need quota negotiation with infra and a tiered sampling strategy after initial pilot.

Next steps (owner: Maya Patel)
- Build small PoC that emits NDJSON evidence for the console service and validate Elastic index (Due: 2024-10-03).
- Create a pilot cohort list and notification templates (Due: 2024-10-10).
- Wire up a Splunk test index and map fields (collab: Rafael Ortiz).
- Schedule tabletop exercises for incident rollback (collab: SRE and Support).

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally lightweight and operational; draft policy mapping rules are in the linked Confluence page. Please comment on: cohort sizing strategy, sampling rate suggestions, and automated QA gating rules.
